text:
maya: heads-up — saw region-level capacity churn for H100 spot pools in us-west1 yesterday, SLOs dipped.
sam: can you paste the numbers? :thinking_face:
maya: 3 evictions in ~2h, median replacement 130s, tail ~600s. cost savings ~48% vs on-demand.
jordan: context — we were using price-optimized across 3 AZs. when market price spiked we lost most nodes in that zone at once.
ellie: proposal: add a tiny warm-buffer of capacity-optimized nodes (worse $/hr but far fewer evictions) to cover hot-path inference.
maya: operational pattern: split pools by intent — price-optimized for experimental/batch, capacity-optimized for hot-path + tiny reserved buffer (~3-5% of baseline).
aaron: also think about soft-eviction TTL: on preempt signal, mark node Draining, attempt graceful migration for up to 90s before hard kill.
sam: how do we detect reliably? cloud metadata hooks + instance lifecycle hook + node-exporter event?
ops-bot: [automated] spot-eviction-alert: h100-us-west1 pool triggered 3 evictions (see https://internal/alerts/123)
jordan: bidding strategy notes: for capacity pool set max-price ~= on-demand (or disable cap on providers that allow it) to maximize allocation probability. price-optimized pools keep max-price ~60-70% to retain savings.
ellie: scheduler changes needed — label nodes as price/capacity/reserved and prefer packing long-running or latency-sensitive jobs onto capacity/reserved. short preemptible jobs go to price-optimized.
maya: fallback plan: if capacity pool can't fulfill, fall back to dedicated reserved capacity (burst group) or to CPU-only inference workers for degraded but available service.
aaron: I'll prototype a terraform module: warm-buffer with autoscaler min=1 max=10, capacity-optimized instance template.
jordan: sample terraform-ish for GCE:
```
resource "google_compute_instance_template" "capacity_opt" {
  scheduling { preemptible = false }
  guest_accelerator { type = "nvidia-tesla-h100" }
}
```
(we'd also have a spot template with preemptible=true and max_price set)
sam: monitoring — add metrics: spot_eviction_count_per_region, avg_replacement_latency, evictions_per_pool. alert if >1.5 evictions/hr or replacement_latency_p95 > 300s.
ellie: and tie quality regressions to these events — post-eviction evaluation to catch model-output drift due to swapped nodes/quant setups.
maya: rollout plan: phase 1 create capacity pools in us-west1 & eu-west1 and shift 5% traffic; phase 2 implement soft-eviction TTL + graceful drain hooks; phase 3 measure cost vs SLO and iterate.
jordan: note: GCP preemptible vs spot semantics differ (preemptible has 24h cap), keep that in mind when planning fallback.
maya: +1 on audit logs for any billing changes and a dashboard for buffer utilization. :thumbsup:
aaron: timeline: prototype by EOD Friday, canary next week.
sam: ack — I'll add the alerts and dashboard PR.
ellie: I'll wire evals to the canary so we measure QoS impact.
maya: thanks all — good plan. moving follow-ups to this thread for action items.
